ledger.x: 500 BC: Monte Albán is founded on an empty hilltop above the Valley of Oaxaca.
100 BC: Monte Albán expands beyond the valley.

c. 500–750: Monte Albán loses its political pre-eminence and the outer valleys fall away. 'The city lost its political pre-eminence by the end of the Late Classic (c. AD 500–750)'. The year 602 is Cliopatria's keyframe inside that window, not the page's; confidence 1.

c. 900: Monte Albán is largely abandoned and the valley's centres go their own way. 'By the end of the same period (c. AD 900–1000), the ancient capital was largely abandoned'; other centres 'began to assert their autonomy, including sites such as Cuilapan and Zaachila in the Valle Grande' and 'Lambityeco, Mitla, and…

wars.name: Monte Albán II conquests (Building J slabs)
wars.outcome: Monte Albán incorporated the Cañada de Cuicatlán and the Ejutla and Sola de Vega valleys 'militarily, through cooption, and via outright colonization'; 'Some of the places listed on Building J slabs have been tentatively identified'.
